Day 5, afternoon and evening. The family sat to supper all together for the first time since he left — [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO] still dusty from the hill, his plate filled without his being asked, Marcos silent in the corner chair with one hand on his walking stick and his eyes on the boy. His mother said he would want to tell Rosa everything, and he said she would not forgive him if he didn't. Eating, he thought about the night on the far side: the sun touching the horizon, Clara opening the door, Elena there, and the dark closing round a bed that was not his — and how it had not swallowed him. When the light came back he was still himself.

Afterwards there were figs, and he excused himself and went up in the half-dark. Bruno was waiting on the bed. He jumped down and circled three times, the way he does everywhere, but there was no tension in it — tail straight, ears forward, his body not coiled and waiting — and [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO] could feel the difference. The night was an ordinary night for Bruno, so it was an ordinary night.

By the last of the light he opened the leather notebook to a fresh page and wrote: "Elena has a fossil too. We are the same kind of person."

Nothing is open. Captain Crunch is on the shelf above his desk; Elena has the striped grey stone.
